{{Short description|German microbiologist}}
'''Alexander von Gabain''' is a microbiologist, academic, founder of several biotech firms and board member of venture capital firms. He has worked at the intersection of the healthcare industry, academia and research throughout his career. He was one of the founding board members of [[European Institute of Innovation and Technology|EIT]] in 2008<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Official appointment of the EIT Governing Board: the European Institute of Innovation and Technology set for an Autumn launch in Budapest|url=https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/IP_08_1220|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201025121843/https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/IP_08_1220 |archive-date=2020-10-25 }}</ref> and began his involvement in [[EIT Health]] in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Science Business|url=https://sciencebusiness.net/network-news/eit-health-appoints-alexander-von-gabain-supervisory-board-chairman|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171019131139/https://sciencebusiness.net/network-news/eit-health-appoints-alexander-von-gabain-supervisory-board-chairman |archive-date=2017-10-19 }}</ref>

His passion for biomedical research and innovation, particularly in the fields of microbiology, immunology and vaccines, has been well-documented through numerous publications;<ref>{{Cite web|title=von Gabain a - Search Results - PubMed|url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=von+Gabain+a|access-date=2021-12-20|website=PubMed|language=en}}</ref> and his achievements in these fields have been well-recognised through industrial awards, academic prizes and honourable memberships. 
 
==Academic background==
von Gabain obtained his PhD in [[Genetics]] at the [[University of Heidelberg]] and held a post-doctorate position at [[Stanford University]] from 1979 to 1982.<ref name=":1"/>

In the 1980s and 1990s, he was Professor at the [[University of Umeå]] and at the [[Karolinska Institute]] in Stockholm, Sweden, as well as an advisor to pharmaceutical and biotech companies. From 1993 to 1999, he was chair of [[Microbiology]] of the [[University of Vienna]] and engaged in building the public-private partnership between the Vienna-based universities and [[Boehringer Ingelheim]] known as [[Vienna Biocenter]].<ref name=":1"/>

His current academic appointments include as a member of the Scientific Advisory Board of the [[Paul Ehrlich Institute]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Scientific Advisory Board of Paul-Ehrlich Institute|url=https://www.pei.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/institute/scientific-advisory-board/scientific-advisory-board.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=2|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420173614/https://www.pei.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/institute/scientific-advisory-board/scientific-advisory-board.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=2 |archive-date=2021-04-20 }}</ref> a member of the Board of Trustees of the [[Institute of Science and Technology Austria]] (ISTA),<ref>{{Cite web|title=Board of Trustees of IST Austria|url=https://ist.ac.at/en/institute/organization/boards/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200504031441/https://ist.ac.at/en/institute/organization/boards/ |archive-date=2020-05-04 }}</ref> a member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=International Fellows of the Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences|url=https://www.iva.se/en/About-IVA/internationalaffairs/international-fellows/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925132623/https://www.iva.se/en/About-IVA/internationalaffairs/international-fellows/ |archive-date=2020-09-25 }}</ref> and a Professor Emeritus for Microbiology at the [[Max F. Perutz Laboratories]], a center established by the [[University of Vienna]] and the [[Medical University of Vienna]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=ResearchGate.net Profile|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Alexander-Von-Gabain|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211220092422/https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Alexander-Von-Gabain |archive-date=2021-12-20 }}</ref> He also serves as Vice-President Emeritus at the [[Karolinska Institute]] in Stockholm,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=CV from EIT Health|url=https://eithealth.eu/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/Alexander-von-Gabain-CV-1.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201231063244/https://eithealth.eu/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/Alexander-von-Gabain-CV-1.pdf |archive-date=2020-12-31 }}</ref> having served as Deputy Vice-Chancellor for Innovation and Commercial Outreach between 2014 and 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Karolinska Institutet News Article|url=https://nyheter.ki.se/karolinska-institutet-rekryterar-internationell-innovations-och-affarsutvecklare-av-toppklass|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211220092353/https://nyheter.ki.se/karolinska-institutet-rekryterar-internationell-innovations-och-affarsutvecklare-av-toppklass |archive-date=2021-12-20 }}</ref>

==Intercell and other innovation work==
von Gabain co-founded [[Intercell AG]] in 1998, led the company until it was successfully floated on the [[Vienna Stock Exchange]] in 2005[[Alexander von Gabain#cite note-1|<sup>[</sup>]]<ref>{{Cite web|date=January 2005|title=Life Science Austria - Vienna Region's Newsletter|url=https://www.lisavienna.at/fileadmin/user_upload/LISAvienna/Downloads/newsletter_01_2005_0_0.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191015205602/https://www.lisavienna.at/fileadmin/user_upload/LISAvienna/Downloads/newsletter_01_2005_0_0.pdf |archive-date=2019-10-15 }}</ref>[[Alexander von Gabain#cite note-1|<sup><nowiki>1]</nowiki></sup>]] and continued as Chief Scientific Officer in the Executive Board until 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|date=April 2010|title=Intercell Geschäftsbericht 2009v|url=https://issuu.com/boerseexpress/docs/2009_annual_report|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100506070507/http://issuu.com/boerseexpress/docs/2009_annual_report|archive-date=2010-05-06|access-date=2021-12-20}}</ref> In 2011, he was appointed to the company's Supervisory Board<ref>{{Cite web|title=Intercell Press Release|date=5 May 2011 |url=https://www.fiercebiotech.com/biotech/intercell-announces-new-management-structure|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200815164024/https://www.fiercebiotech.com/biotech/intercell-announces-new-management-structure |archive-date=2020-08-15 }}</ref> and continues to hold this position after it Intercell and Vivalis merged into the trans-European biotech enterprise, Valneva, listed on [[Euronext Paris]] since 2013<ref>{{Cite web|title=Valneva Press Information|url=https://valneva.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/FAQ_VSE_Delisting.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211220092353/https://valneva.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/FAQ_VSE_Delisting.pdf |archive-date=2021-12-20 }}</ref> and on [[Nasdaq]] since 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Valneva Press Release|url=https://valneva.com/press-release/valneva-announces-the-pricing-of-its-initial-public-offering-on-nasdaq/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506172216/https://valneva.com/press-release/valneva-announces-the-pricing-of-its-initial-public-offering-on-nasdaq/ |archive-date=2021-05-06 }}</ref> [[Valneva SE|Valneva]] has today two global vaccines on the market, more than 600 employees and three major vaccines in late clinical development.

Additionally, he has supported other biotech enterprises and related VC firms in various functions. His entrepreneurial and scientific knowledge in the [[innovation]] arena has been highly sought after by organisations fostering entrepreneurial innovation. Between 2007 and 2019, he was Chair of INiTS, the technology seed fund and incubator of the [[University of Vienna]] and the [[TU Wien|Technical University of Vienna]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=INiTS Universitäres Gründerservice Wien congratulates Sabine Seidler, Heinz Engl and Alexander von Gabain|url=https://www.ots.at/presseaussendung/OTS_20110310_OTS0036/inits-universitaeres-gruenderservice-wien-gratuliert-sabine-seidler-heinz-engl-und-alexander-von-gabain|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211220092356/https://www.ots.at/presseaussendung/OTS_20110310_OTS0036/inits-universitaeres-gruenderservice-wien-gratuliert-sabine-seidler-heinz-engl-und-alexander-von-gabain |archive-date=2021-12-20 }}</ref> initiating more than 300 start-ups and ranking amongst the top ten of university incubators globally.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wiener INiTS in den Top 10 der Uni-Inkubatoren|date=27 November 2015 |url=https://brutkasten.com/wiener-inits-in-den-top-10-der-uni-inkubatoren/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211220092423/https://brutkasten.com/wiener-inits-in-den-top-10-der-uni-inkubatoren/ |archive-date=2021-12-20 }}</ref> He is currently a member of the Supervisory Board of [https://www.eveliqure.com/ Eveliqure]- an innovative biotech company developing novel vaccines for the prevention of diarrhoeal disease,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Eveliqure Board|url=https://www.eveliqure.com/board|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200807090346/https://www.eveliqure.com/board |archive-date=2020-08-07 }}</ref> a member of the Supervisory Board of [https://biocopy.ch/ Biocopy]- whose patented biomolecule copier is used for the production and replication of all kinds of different microarrays.<ref>{{Cite web|title=BioCopy AG|url=https://biocopy.ch/company/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200815020314/https://biocopy.ch/company/ |archive-date=2020-08-15 }}</ref>

==EIT and EIT Health==
In 2008, he was appointed as a founding member of the Governing Board of the [[European Institute of Innovation and Technology]] (EIT)<ref name=":0"/> and in 2011 was elected to become its Chairman for a period ending in 2014.<ref name=":1"/><ref>{{Cite web|title=Alexander von Gabain starts as Chairman of the EIT Governing Board|date=14 September 2011 |url=https://eit.europa.eu/news-events/news/alexander-von-gabain-starts-chairman-eit-governing-board|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190615091708/https://eit.europa.eu/news-events/news/alexander-von-gabain-starts-chairman-eit-governing-board |archive-date=2019-06-15 }}</ref> During this time, the first three of EIT's Knowledge and Innovation Communities (KICs) were established and EIT evolved into a multi-billion dollar organisation.

In 2015, he joined the Supervisory Board of EIT Health<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.eithealth.eu/ |title=Home |website=eithealth.eu}}</ref> - an innovation consortium with more than 150 leading organisations and institutions from the European healthcare space.<ref name=":1"/> In 2017, he was appointed Chair of the organisations Supervisory Board,<ref>{{Cite web|title=EIT Health appoints Alexander von Gabain Supervisory Board Chairman|url=https://sciencebusiness.net/network-news/eit-health-appoints-alexander-von-gabain-supervisory-board-chairman|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171019131139/https://sciencebusiness.net/network-news/eit-health-appoints-alexander-von-gabain-supervisory-board-chairman |archive-date=2017-10-19 }}</ref> a position he held until 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=EIT Health announces new Supervisory Board|url=https://eithealth.eu/news-article/new-supervisory-board/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210928154949/https://eithealth.eu/news-article/new-supervisory-board/ |archive-date=2021-09-28 }}</ref>
